newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-LANGUID SPANIARD BECOMES MELBOURNE'S NEW PIN-UP.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-LANGUID SPANIARD BECOMES MELBOURNE'S NEW PIN-UP.

text.p: With most of the hometown heroes already defeated, fickle female fans at the Australian Open have found a new idol.
They had wanted to cheer for Mark Philippoussis, the darkly handsome local boy with a big serve, but he dropped out on Sunday with a sore arm.
Then they chose Patrick Rafter, a blue-eyed Queenslander and part-time model. Rafter was eliminated on Tuesday night.
So the Melbourne teenies had to find a new pin-up, and on Wednesday their choice became clear: Spanish giant-killer Carlos Moya.

They were there on court number three as Moya, who ousted defending champion Boris Becker on Monday, fought American Patrick McEnroe, cheering him on point-by-point as he came back from a one-set deficit to win 3-6 6-0 6-3 6-1.
His victory complete, a crowd of teenage girls waited for autographs as the tanned Spaniard, his long brown hair tied into a pony-tail, left the court.
"I'm the first to be surprised how the crowd they want me and it's nice to feel," the 20-year-old baseliner, who comes from the Spanish resort island of Majorca, told reporters.
"I like to thank them that they are supporting me a lot and it's very good for me. Even when I was one set down they support me and they help me a lot," he said.

Moya is not the only Spaniard playing well in Melbourne. There are more than a dozen Spaniards in the men's top 100, including seeds Albert Costa, Felix Mantilla and Alberto Berasategui, all of them winners so far.
But Moya, who is 1.90 metres (six foot three inches) tall and describes himself as a fan of Irish rock group U2, is the one the teenies have adopted.
Melbourne's Herald Sun daily tabloid newspaper reported on Wednesday that a straw poll at the championship showed Moya was the fans' pin-up choice -- and not just among the girls.
"It isn't the same here without Stefan (Edberg) but Moya is a fair replacement," Craig, a local gay who has been a fan of the Melbourne men's draw for 10 years, told the newspaper.
